source.author: hor
source.text: difficile est proprie communia dicere, tuque rectius Iliacum carmen deducis in actus quam si proferres ignota indictaque primus: publica materies privati iuris erit, si non circa vilem patulumque moraberis orbem nec verbo verbum curabis reddere fidus interpres nec desilies imitator in artum, unde pedem proferre pudor vetet aut operis lex, nec sic incipies, ut scriptor cyclicus olim: fortunam Priami cantabo et nobile bellum.
source.text_original: difficile est proprie communia dicere, tuque  / rectius Iliacum carmen deducis in actus  / quam si proferres ignota indictaque primus:  / publica materies privati iuris erit, si  / non circa vilem patulumque moraberis orbem  / nec verbo verbum curabis reddere fidus  / interpres nec desilies imitator in artum,  / unde pedem proferre pudor vetet aut operis lex,  / nec sic incipies, ut scriptor cyclicus olim:  / 'fortunam Priami cantabo et nobile bellum.'
source.text_english: It is difficult to speak of common things in a distinctive way, and you do better to turn an Iliac poem into acts than if you were to bring forward things unknown and untried for the first time; a subject matter in common will become your private property, if you do not linger around a base and broad simple road, and if, as a faithful interpreter, you do not take care to render word for word, and if, as an imitator, you do not leap into a narrow place from which shame or the law of the work forbids you to move your foot, and if you do not begin as that cyclic poet once did: I will sing of the fate of Priam and the noble war.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: sed et Horatius, uir acutus et doctus, hoc idem in Arte poetica erudito interpreti praecipit: nec uerbum uerbo curabis reddere fidus interpres.
reuse.text_original: sed et Horatius, uir acutus et doctus, hoc idem in Arte poetica erudito interpreti praecipit: nec uerbum uerbo curabis reddere fidus interpres.
reuse.text_english: But Horace too, a sharp and learned man, gives the same instruction in the Art of Poetry to the learned translator: a faithful translator will not be concerned to render word for word.
